newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed, Banco Ganadero falls.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed, Banco Ganadero falls.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed mixed after blue-chip Banco Ganadero was hit by a wave of profit- taking following Tuesday's completion of the sale of a 40 percent stake in the bank to Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up a thin 0.17 percent to close at 13,216.48 on a volume of 1.01 billion pesos. But Bogota's IBB dropped 1.09 percent to end at 842.56 on a lackluster volume of 589.8 million pesos.
Ganadero accounted for the bulk of the volume in Bogota. Ordinary shares fell for the second consecutive day, shedding 2.43 percent of their value to end at 280 pesos per share.
As part of its previously agreed merger with Ganadero, Bilbao Vizcaya completed its purchase Tuesday of 425.62 million already issued ordinary shares at 295 pesos per share.
"It was convenient for anyone who held onto his shares yesterday to sell them today," one broker said.

Ganadero took an even bigger hit in Medellin, dropping 3.30 percent to end at 278 pesos per share. The day's winners included Banco de Colombia, which rose 0.47 percent in Bogota to close at 422 pesos a share. Cementos Caribe also ended up in Bogota, gaining 0.52 percent to close at 3,820 pesos a share.
The day's biggest gainer was in Medellin, however, where Banco Industrial Colombiano rose 2.94 percent to close at 3,500 pesos a share.
The bank's rise was attributed by Jaime Jaramillio of Casa de Bolsa in Medellin to "people who sold Ganadero shares but didn't want to pull out the market completely."

Jaramillo said stocks were expected to remain mostly flat in the near-term. But he added that they could get a boost if the government manages to put downward pressure on interest rates, which continue to put a premium on fixed-income investment over equities
